Answer: C
Reason: The clinical context of a rapid drop in end-tidal CO2 during vertebroplasty strongly suggests pulmonary cement embolism, and the provided CT images (Figures 4a/4b) clearly show hyperdense material within the pulmonary arteries consistent with polymethylmethacrylate (PMMA) emboli. While the chest X-ray findings can be subtle, the presence of these radiopaque emboli on cross-sectional imaging confirms the diagnosis described in option C.
